205626: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was discovered in the website translate-coursera.org. By inserting malicious JavaScript code into the first name field when creating an account on coursera.org, an attacker could execute the code when the victim visits translate-coursera.org after logging in. This allows the attacker to steal session cookies and take over the account. The vulnerability allows arbitrary JavaScript to be executed and should be fixed to prevent compromise of user accounts.
245304: A vulnerability was found that allowed multiple accounts to be created using a single email address on a website. By registering two accounts with the same email on different browsers, adding that email as an additional association to one account after initially disconnecting it, and filling the password, both accounts could be accessed with the same email. This led to server errors when logging out of either account.
285609: The html editor allowed the frameset and frame html tags, which could have led to clickjacking.
301526: The invitation page on HackerOne contained iframes that pointed to specific endpoints. When a GET request was made to these endpoints, a script was executed that pointed to `https://bat.bing.com/bat.js`. The corresponding request to bing contained the invitation tokens, potentially leaking sensitive information.
415622: The vulnerability allowed past team members of a partner team, including those without explicit permissions, to have their personal email IDs and removal dates disclosed to current team members through the Partner Dashboard. Additionally, if a past team member changed their email ID and name on their Shopify account, that updated information could be viewed by current team members.
419896: The vulnerability allowed an unauthenticated user to upload attachments and attach them to the last created report draft of other users by sending a specially crafted request to the `/attachments` endpoint. The vulnerability was identified by HackerOne and a report was filed to their own bug bounty program. The vulnerability was retested by the community, and the investigation concluded that it was not abused.
438953: A cross-site scripting vulnerability was found in a website's API that allowed HTTP requests to be manipulated. This could have enabled malicious users to inject client-side scripts and potentially steal user credentials or modify content seen by users.
